prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: システム連携用語表 (language ja).
Grid: 3 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "用語" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 210px
  col 2: header "英語" · longest unbreakable word 103px · one-line width 163px
  col 3: header "説明" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 860px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A bilingual glossary for system-integration terms: readers identify a Japanese term, map it to its English equivalent, and read a short definition.","reading":"Scan down column 1 for the term, compare across to column 2 for the English label, then read column 3. Rows are the unit of comparison, so stable row starts and a readable term/translation pair matter more than equal column widths.","groups":["Columns 1–2 form the term/translation lookup pair and should stay adjacent with related widths.","Column 3 is a separate explanatory field and can absorb most wrapping."],"keep_intact":["English unbreakable tokens; column 2 needs at least 124px total for the 103px longest word.","Japanese terms as whole lookup keys where possible, ideally without splitting across more than 2–3 lines.","Headers 用語 / 英語 / 説明."],"may_wrap":["Column 3 descriptions at natural Japanese line breaks.","Multi-word English phrases at spaces, e.g. transaction manager / service level agreement.","Long Japanese terms at character boundaries only when necessary."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[115,124,120],"idea":"A balanced mobile layout that keeps the term/translation pair readable while giving the explanation a workable middle width."},{"name":"B","widths":[145,124,90],"idea":"Prioritize the Japanese term and English label for fast lookup, accepting a narrower, taller description column."},{"name":"C","widths":[90,124,145],"idea":"Give the explanation the largest share for prose readability, letting Japanese terms wrap more aggressively."}]}
